videos.title: Bästa fonderna för pensionen?
videos.summary_source_text:
Bästa fonderna för pensionen? Marie har 18 år kvar till pension och undrar vilken fond hon ska välja.

Svaret är samma som i våras, samma som förra året, och samma som för tio år sedan. Ingenting har förändrats.

Forskningen är ganska entydig om vad som har bäst odds framgent:

- Bred
- Billig
- Global
- Passiv indexfond

Alltså: äg hela höstacken i stället för att leta nålarna. Då får du med nålarna på vägen.

Helt konkret: gå till din bank eller din valcentral och leta efter en fond som har global i namnet, har index i namnet och kostar under 0,2 procent. Hittar du ingen finns vår lista per bank på rikatillsammans.se under Spara och investera, Bästa fonderna.

Och eftersom vi pratar konkret fond: historisk avkastning är ingen garanti för framtida avkastning. Du kan förlora delar av eller hela ditt kapital. Läs riskinformationen.

If You Eat Eggs, You Need to Know This About Your Arteries | Dr. Mandell Are eggs really clogging your arteries, or is there much more to the story? For years, eggs and dietary cholesterol have been at the center of the heart-health debate, but cardiovascular health is influenced by far more than any single food. In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell explains what happens inside your arteries, how atherosclerotic plaque develops, and why factors such as elevated LDL cholesterol, high blood sugar, inflammation, smoking, high blood pressure, physical inactivity, poor sleep, chronic stress, and the overall quality of your diet can all play important roles in cardiovascular health. You’ll also learn about the nutritional value of eggs, including high-quality protein and choline, and why the effect of eggs should be considered in the context of your complete eating pattern and your individual health and cholesterol levels. The goal is not to fear one particular food, but to better understand the bigger picture and make informed choices that help protect your heart, blood vessels, circulation, brain, and long-term health. If you eat eggs—or you've ever wondered whether you should—this information can help you better understand the relationship between eggs, cholesterol, and your arteries. videos.title: Gemini 4 Pro Just Leaked: The Results Are Insane
videos.summary_source_text:
Gemini 4 Pro Just Leaked: The Results Are Insane Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/

A mysterious Gemini model started producing surprisingly advanced interactive games and SVG demos inside Arena — while being labeled as the already-released Gemini 3.8 Flash. Just days earlier, an X account claimed to have leaked Gemini 4 Pro under the internal codename “Argon,” with a massive 2-million-token context window and 256,000-token output limit.

So did Google quietly put Gemini 4 Pro into Arena for public testing, or is the internet connecting dots that were never connected?

The mystery started with unusually capable Arena outputs: an interactive pelican riding a bicycle, a teapot with working controls, and eventually a playable Ultraman-versus-Godzilla browser game complete with animations, enemies, lasers, and a functioning score counter. Every one of these outputs appeared under the Gemini 3.8 Flash name.

That immediately fueled speculation that Google was disguising an unreleased Gemini 4 checkpoint.

And the timing made the theory even more compelling. Three days before the Arena sightings, the X account Lentils80 posted what it claimed was the first leaked output from Gemini 4 Pro “Argon.” The alleged model reportedly had a 2-million-token context window and 256K output ceiling — dramatically beyond the documented Gemini 3.8 Flash limits.

But there’s a major problem: none of those Argon specifications have been independently verified.

Google has confirmed that Gemini 4 exists only in a much narrower sense. Sundar Pichai said in July that Google DeepMind had begun its “most ambitious pre-training run yet for Gemini 4.” Google did not confirm a Gemini 4 Pro model, the Argon codename, those leaked specifications, or a release date.

There’s also precedent for fake Gemini 4 leaks. An August “Gemini 4 Pro benchmark” supposedly showed extraordinary scores, including 99.9% on ARC-AGI-3. Those numbers were later found to match published results attributed to a competing OpenAI model, suggesting the supposed Gemini benchmark had simply been relabeled.

Then comes potentially the biggest problem for the Argon theory.

At least one Arena tester reportedly reproduced the mysterious output quality by selecting “gemini-3.8-flash-high” — a higher-thinking configuration of the existing Gemini 3.8 Flash model. There’s also a significant speed mismatch: the alleged Argon generation reportedly took 2.4 minutes, while some supposed Gemini 4 comparisons took far longer. The mysterious Arena demos could return in seconds.

There’s no “Argon” fingerprint hidden in the generated code, no leaked model card, no API listing, and no Gemini 4 entry on Arena’s scored leaderboard.

Still, the creative coding performance is difficult to ignore. The model produced polished, interactive experiences that surprised testers and generated comparisons with other frontier models. Something about these outputs caught the community’s attention — the unresolved question is whether that “something” is a secret Gemini 4 checkpoint, a higher-reasoning Gemini 3.8 Flash configuration, narrow optimization, or something else entirely.

We break down the Arena sightings, the Argon leak, the evidence for and against the Gemini 4 theory, the previously debunked benchmark leak, and exactly what Google has — and hasn’t — officially confirmed.

02:02 The Arena Sightings
04:05 The Argon Leak
06:03 Is This Actually A New Model?
08:42 The Case For And The Case Against
11:19 What We Still Don't Know

videos.title: Grok 4.7 Just Dropped… This Is a BIG Upgrade
videos.summary_source_text:
Grok 4.7 Just Dropped… This Is a BIG Upgrade Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/

Grok 4.7 just jumped from 31.9% to 46.0% on SWE-Marathon — a 44% relative improvement in just six weeks. But when independent lab Artificial Analysis tested xAI’s new model, its composite score moved from 44 to just 46… while generating more than twice as many output tokens.

That gap between xAI’s headline benchmarks and independent testing is where Grok 4.7 gets interesting.

xAI announced Grok 4.7 on September 21, 2026, just 40 days after Grok 4.6. According to xAI, this is a new, larger base model with longer supplemental training, curated reasoning data, advanced technical corpora, an improved training recipe, and heavier reinforcement learning on difficult multi-hour agentic tasks.

But most regular Grok users can’t actually use it yet. Grok 4.7 launched through the xAI API, Grok Build, Cursor, and Microsoft Office add-ins first, while access through Grok’s web and mobile apps and Grok on X is coming later.

The headline improvements are concentrated around coding and long-running agents. We break down DeepSWE, Terminal-Bench 4.0, FrontierSWE V2, SWE-Marathon, and CursorBench 4.0 individually — including where Grok 4.7 makes clean gains and where reasoning-effort differences make xAI’s comparisons less straightforward.

There are some impressive numbers. Grok 4.7 reaches 71.0% on DeepSWE and jumps to 46.0% on SWE-Marathon. But competitors including GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Fable 5.1, and Opus 5 still lead several of these coding benchmarks.

The bigger story may be agents that can work for hours. xAI tested Grok 4.7 on software engineering tasks with time budgets reaching 20 hours and is increasingly positioning Grok for professional work beyond coding: legal documents, spreadsheets, presentations, CAD, electrical engineering, biological data, and other complex workflows.

Then comes the independent reality check.

Artificial Analysis scored Grok 4.7 high at 46 on its Intelligence Index, compared with 44 for Grok 4.6 high. But its evaluation produced roughly 200 million output tokens for 4.7 versus about 94 million for 4.6. Measured cost per evaluated task also increased from $1.86 to $2.73. Same list price per token does not necessarily mean the same cost per completed task.

Pricing itself remains $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens for standard requests at or below 200,000 tokens. Go beyond that threshold and the entire request moves to the higher long-context pricing tier. We compare that with GPT-6 Astra, GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Fable 5.1, and Gemini 3.8 Flash — and look at whether Grok can still claim a meaningful price advantage.

We also dig into xAI’s safety card. Several jailbreak and harmful-compliance measurements improved, while general harmful-request compliance and the self-harm metric moved slightly in the wrong direction. Some biosecurity-related capability scores also declined intentionally, according to xAI, as part of its safety training approach.

And there are still major unanswered questions: no parameter count, no disclosed dense-vs-MoE architecture, no training compute or cost, no standalone long-context benchmark, and no general computer-use tool.

Grok 4.7 is clearly more than a rename. The question is whether its gains justify how much more inference it may need to produce them.

CHAPTERS

00:00 Grok 4.7’s Huge Benchmark Jump Has a Catch
01:12 What Actually Shipped, and Where You Can't Use It Yet
02:42 What xAI Actually Changed Under the Hood
04:22 The Coding Benchmarks, One at a Time
06:58 Agents That Work for Hours, and the Push Into Professional Work
09:06 The Independent Reality Check
11:09 The Price Tag, and the Fine Print xAI Didn't Put in the Headline
13:00 What Got Safer, and What Quietly Got Worse
14:30 What xAI Still Won't Tell You

100 000:- under Volvo EX30 – kap eller skräp? Provkörning av Leapmotor B05. Leapmotor B05 krossar konkurrenterna när vi ser till hårdvara. För nästan 130 000 kr mindre än en räckviddsmatchad Volvo EX30 får du en bil som är 20 centimeter längre och faktiskt har ett fungerande baksäte, som dessutom laddar snabbare. Volvon är i princip oanvändbar bakom en lång förare.

ID. Polo imponerar rejält med 435 liters bagageutrymme, vilket slår båda de längre bilarna. Men instegsmodellen för 320 900 kr är strypt till 38,5 kWh användbart batteri, 30 mils räckvidd och har en maxladdning på extremt låga 90 kW. För att nå 450 km drar prislappen på folkan iväg kraftigt.

Jag provkör nya Leapmotor B05 och hittar en hel del nackdelar som man kanske inte kan leva med? Jag har också studerat värdefall och jämför privatleasingpriser och intervjuar Leapmotors svenska marknadschef - och tittar på nya lilla Leapmotor B03X. 


                                    Leapmotor B05                 Volvo EX30                    VW ID. Polo
                                                                                Single Motor ER             85 kW / 38,5 kWh
Längd                         443 cm                              423 cm                            405 cm
Bagage / Frunk         345 liter / Saknas            318 liter / 7 liter             435 liter / Saknas 
Räckvidd (WLTP)     482 km                               476 km                            300 km
Max laddning (DC).  174 kW                               153 kW                            90 kW
Pris (från)                  359 900 kr                          489 000 kr                      320 900 kr

Don't Use Weight Transfers Drop Your Hip Instead The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

What are the four fundamentals that matter most for becoming a better golfer? In this video, we break down the key positions and movements that can have the biggest impact on your ball striking: setup, club path, clubface, and keeping the club in front of you throughout the swing.

You’ll learn why club path is one of the most common problems golfers struggle with, how an outside-in or overly inside path can lead to slices, hooks, shanks, fat shots, and tops, and how simple alignment-stick drills can help you improve your path. We also look at the importance of a square clubface, including how small changes in clubface position during the backswing can dramatically affect ball flight.

Finally, we get into the foundation of the entire swing: your setup. Proper distance from the ball, alignment, ball position, and grip all influence your ability to swing the club correctly. The fourth fundamental—keeping the club in front of you—can also help improve both your path and clubface. Finally, we get into the foundation of the entire swing: your setup. Proper distance from the ball, alignment, ball position, and grip all influence your ability to swing the club correctly. The fourth fundamental—keeping the club in front of you—can also help improve both your path and clubface. If you're trying to hit the ball more consistently and understand the root causes of your swing mistakes, these four fundamentals are a great place to start.

videos.summary_source_text:
INSIDE PATH—STILL SLICING? You can swing from the inside and still hit a huge slice.

Why? Because fixing your club path is only half the equation. If the clubface stays open relative to that path, the ball can start right and curve even farther right.

The goal isn’t just to swing from the inside, it’s to match your clubface to your path through impact.
That’s where the Blue Brick can help. It gives you a clear visual reference for your swing direction, helping you build an inside path you can repeat while learning to deliver the club more consistently. Instead of guessing what your club is doing, you can see it and train it.

Fix the path. Match the face. Start hitting straighter, more powerful shots!

videos.title: 483. Niklas Laninge, sparpsykolog, om beteendemisstagen som sabbar avkastningen
videos.summary_source_text:
483. Niklas Laninge, sparpsykolog, om beteendemisstagen som sabbar avkastningen Vad kostar egentligen mest, fonden med fel avgift eller att bli lurad av sin egen hjärna? Det här avsnittet handlar om sparpsykologi, och jag gästas av Niklas Laninge, sparpsykolog på Opti och en uppskattad gäst. Vi pratar om sparmisstagen som aldrig syns på kontot, misstag vi sett hos oss själva och andra sparare och allmänt snack om sparande.

*För tydlighetens skull*: avsnittet är sponsrat av och reklam för fondroboten Opti där Niklas arbetar till vardags. 

Huvudpoängen är enkel och på många sätt jobbig: sparande handlar mer psykologi och beteende än ekonomi. De dyraste misstagen är inte de aktiva valen utan tankefällorna vi inte ser och tillsammans kostar de uppskattningsvis 1–3 procentenheter om året i avkastning. 

Vi pratar om varför vi inte kan låta sparandet vara i fred, varför identitet ofta styr mer än avkastning och varför så få vågar använda pengarna när de väl är sparade. Det är ett samtal lika mycket om att våga låta bli att agera som om att våga spendera.

Några av ämnena vi tar upp i veckans avsnitt är:

• Varför sparande är mer psykologi än ekonomi
• Self-serving bias, alltså idén att tankefällorna gäller alla andra utom mig
• Action bias och varför det ofta lönar sig att låta bli på börsen
• Att vi investerar lika mycket av identitet som för avkastningens skull
• Exponential growth bias och vad 100 000 kronor faktiskt kan bli på 30 år
• Konsten att våga spendera i pensionen i stället för att dö som rikast på kyrkogården
• Risk som en upplevelse snarare än ett objektivt mått
• Varför en fondrobot passar både nybörjaren och den erfarna spararen

Vi hoppas att du gillar avsnittet,
Jan och Niklas

Innehållsförteckning och kapitel:
====
00:00:00 – Introduktion till avsnittet
00:02:16 – Sparande är mer psykologi än ekonomi, och Dunning-Kruger-effekten
00:07:38 – Beteendemisstag och self-serving bias kostar 1–3 procentenheter
00:11:14 – Action bias: varför vi handlar när vi egentligen borde vänta
00:14:20 – Fel val som ser rätt ut: PPM och riskfria placeringar
00:16:36 – Tre motiv att investera: nyttomaximering, känsloutsläpp och identitet
00:20:10 – Pengar och identitet: vi erkänner sällan vad som egentligen driver oss
00:23:40 – Alternativ till aktier: identitet, risksug och krypto
00:28:57 – Outcome bias: vi utvärderar beslut på utfall snarare än process
00:32:12 – Även indexfondsparare gör aktiva avsteg utan att inse det
00:35:41 – Bekräftelseeffekten: hjärnan förstärker tesen, filtrerar bort motbevis
00:40:32 – Charles Ellis: vinn sparandet genom att undvika misstag
00:44:19 – Fondrobotens plats i båda ändarna av sparresan
00:49:24 – Exponential growth bias: vi underskattar vad pengar faktiskt kan bli
00:54:01 – Räkneexempel: att faktiskt leva på pensionskapitalet, Galápagos-resan
00:57:06 – Fondrobotens avgift i perspektiv mot beteendegapets kostnad
01:00:08 – Fondroboten skyddar inte mot uttag, men ger psykologiska påminnelser
01:04:55 – Mental bokföring: pensionärer dör som rikast på kyrkogården
01:11:07 – Värdet av pengar minskar med åldern, arvspsykologi och vanans makt
01:15:58 – Glädjefällan: 12 kronor på rea känns bättre än 50 000 på börsen
01:20:37 – Ekonomibyrån på TV4: fjällsemester, friendflation och jämförelsenormer
01:28:03 – Risktoleransbedömningars brister: attityd och riskuppfattning
01:33:14 – Sämsta råden: bolåneråd och single-action bias
01:35:26 – De tre stora kostnadsposterna och Prius-effekten i Sverige
01:38:06 – Sammanfattning: automatisera sparandet och sluta lura dig själv

Några av ämnena vi tar upp i veckans avsnitt är:

• Varför sparande är mer psykologi än ekonomi
• Self-serving bias, alltså idén att tankefällorna gäller alla andra utom mig
• Action bias och varför det ofta lönar sig att låta bli på börsen
• Att vi investerar lika mycket av identitet som för avkastningens skull
• Exponential growth bias och vad 100 000 kronor faktiskt kan bli på 30 år
• Konsten att våga spendera i pensionen i stället för att dö som rikast på kyrkogården
• Risk som en upplevelse snarare än ett objektivt mått
• Varför en fondrobot passar både nybörjaren och den erfarna spararen

Vi hoppas att du gillar avsnittet,
Jan och Niklas

videos.summary_source_text:
21.09.26 - Rift Education Day RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.title: Fix Your Slice With the 9 & 3 O’Clock Check!!
videos.summary_source_text:
Fix Your Slice With the 9 & 3 O’Clock Check!! If you’re fighting a slice, check your clubface at 9 o’clock and 3 o’clock.
At 9 o’clock, you don’t want the face hanging wide open. Then as you swing through to 3 o’clock, let the club rotate naturally while the path works slightly out to the right.

A lot of golfers try to fix a slice by just swinging farther right, but if the face is still open, the ball is still going right.

Get the face and path working together and you can start turning that slice into a draw.
The Blue Brick makes this easy to practice because it gives you something to swing around. Set it down, let the club work through its natural arc, and miss the brick on the way through.

Want an easy way to work on your club path without thinking about a bunch of positions?
Use the Blue Brick as your reference and practice swinging around it. It gives you instant feedback if your path starts getting off.

4 Shot Releases Every Hockey Player Must Practice The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

The Healthiest Carbohydrate in the World The safest carbohydrates are non-starchy vegetables because they contain very little sugar or starch and a lot of fiber. Unlike sugar and starch, fiber does not break down into glucose and has very little effect on insulin.

Carbohydrates come in three forms:
• Sugar
• Starch
• Fiber

Starch is essentially chains of sugar molecules, which is why foods like bread can quickly start tasting sweet as enzymes in your mouth break the starch down.

Non-starchy vegetables like broccoli sit very low on the glycemic index because they’re high in fiber and low in starch. This makes them one of the best carbohydrate choices for keeping blood sugar and insulin more stable.

videos.summary_source_text:
How To Give Your Players Free Speed The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: Your Second Heart Is in Your Legs — Do This Every Day | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
Your Second Heart Is in Your Legs — Do This Every Day | Dr. Mandell Most people have no idea that they have what is often called a “second heart” working inside their legs. The muscles of your calves—particularly the soleus and gastrocnemius—do much more than help you stand and walk. Each time these muscles contract, they help squeeze the veins of the lower legs and assist blood in moving upward against gravity and back toward the heart. When we spend hours sitting, driving, working at a computer, or simply not moving enough, this important calf muscle pump gets far less activity. In this video, Dr. Mandell demonstrates a simple movement you can do every day to activate these muscles, encourage healthy circulation, and keep your lower legs moving. You’ll learn how the calf pump works with the one-way valves in your veins, why movement can be important for people who experience tired or heavy legs after prolonged sitting or standing, and how the deeper soleus muscle has attracted scientific attention for another fascinating reason: metabolism. Research has shown that a specific type of sustained soleus contraction performed while sitting can substantially increase local oxidative metabolism and improve post-meal glucose and insulin responses. This doesn’t replace regular exercise or medical treatment, but it demonstrates just how metabolically active this small muscle can be when used correctly. Whether you spend your day sitting at a desk, standing for long periods, traveling, or simply want to keep your legs active as you age, this is an easy movement to learn and incorporate into your daily routine. Your calves aren't just muscles that move your feet—they're an important part of the circulation system that helps move blood back toward your heart. Start using them every day and keep your body moving from the ground up.

SCIENTIFIC REFERENCES:

videos.title: GPT-6 Astra Just Made the AGI Debate REAL
videos.summary_source_text:
GPT-6 Astra Just Made the AGI Debate REAL Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/

OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra scored an almost unbelievable 99.95% on ARC-AGI-3 — a benchmark designed to test whether AI can learn genuinely unfamiliar tasks. But change the testing harness, and that same model drops to 62.71%.

That gap might tell us more about the state of AGI than the headline score itself.

GPT-6 Astra is OpenAI’s new flagship model, and its capabilities are difficult to dismiss. It can operate real software, build and debug programs, work inside Blender, Unreal Engine and KiCad, browse the web, and tackle research-level mathematics. Under a controlled FrontierMath Erdős evaluation, Astra even solved two open mathematical problems that competing frontier models failed to solve.

But the deeper question is whether extraordinary capability is the same thing as general intelligence.

On ARC-AGI-3, Astra’s 99.95% result came through OpenAI’s Provider Adapter, which preserves internal reasoning state and manages context automatically. Through ARC Prize’s provider-neutral Standard harness, it scored 62.71%. ARC creator François Chollet still described Astra’s interactive reasoning as a “step-function change” in capability — but ARC Prize explicitly warns that saturating a bounded benchmark does not prove AGI.

The contradictions continue elsewhere.

Astra scores around 96% on GPQA Diamond, dramatically outperforming the PhD-expert baseline cited by the benchmark creators. Yet on Humanity’s Last Exam with tools, it reaches only 57.2%, while Claude Fable 5.1 scores 65% in OpenAI’s comparison. A model capable of producing formally verified new mathematics can still fail more than 40% of an extremely difficult expert-level exam.

Then there’s Astra as a digital worker.

OpenAI demonstrations show the model building complex projects across Codex, Blender and Unreal Engine 5, inspecting its own work and correcting errors. It has generated a routed PCB inside KiCad and can execute real terminal-based engineering and scientific workflows. But these demonstrations often involve human direction, corrections and scaffolding — very different from handing an autonomous employee a goal and coming back days later.

That distinction becomes critical because OpenAI’s own Charter defines AGI as “highly autonomous systems that outperform humans at most economically valuable work.”

The autonomy evidence isn't there yet.

A UK AISI evaluation put Astra’s 50%-reliability mathematics time horizon at roughly 30.9 minutes. Artificial Analysis found an approximately 51% hallucination rate at maximum effort on its adversarial AA-Omniscience benchmark. Astra also still fails substantial portions of difficult software and professional-work evaluations.

And cybersecurity introduces another complication. Astra is the first broadly deployed OpenAI model to reach the company’s Critical cybersecurity capability threshold. On fresh vulnerabilities from June through August 2026, it scored 39% versus 5.5% for the previous model and discovered two previously unknown vulnerabilities during testing.

So is GPT-6 Astra actually AGI?

There’s now a serious case that models have crossed into something qualitatively different from the chatbots we were using only a few generations ago. Astra can reason across unfamiliar environments, operate professional tools, perform research-level mathematics and produce useful work across radically different domains.

But there’s an equally serious case that we’re confusing peak intelligence with dependable intelligence. Astra’s performance can change dramatically depending on its scaffolding. It still hallucinates, still fails difficult bounded tasks, and there is no published representative evidence that it can reliably own even a full unsupervised working day across unfamiliar professional goals.

Under a broad definition of general intelligence, the AGI era may have started.

Under OpenAI’s own stricter definition? Not yet.

I Built an INSANELY Profitable AI Trading Bot for FREE (Full Guide) 👉🏻 Learn AI trading bots and algorithmic trading with us:
https://www.skool.com/daviddtech/about

Impressive equity curves are easy to share. This video shows you how to build the system behind them.

I built an AI trading desk with Hermes Agent that can research trading ideas, develop strategies, backtest them, and organize the results in a custom Mission Control dashboard.

In this full guide, I take you through the setup step by step: installing Hermes, connecting an AI model, adding the TradingKit backtesting tools, building your agent team, and creating your own control panel.

Then I show you how to take the resulting Pine Script into TradingView, check the backtest, and connect strategy alerts to a broker through Trigger.trade.

But finding an impressive backtest is only part of the process.

After more than five years of building and testing automated trading systems, I’ve tested over 2,000 strategies and currently trade seven. At the end, I explain what that experience has taught me about selecting strategies and deciding what deserves further testing.

## In this video, you’ll discover:

✅ How to install Hermes Agent and complete the initial setup
✅ How I connect my existing ChatGPT subscription and select GPT-6 Astra
✅ How to set up Telegram and use the Hermes desktop interface
✅ How to connect TradingKit’s backtesting tools through an MCP server
✅ How to run an initial BTCUSDT strategy backtest
✅ How to build an AI trading research team with reusable prompts
✅ How I structure agents and schedules to reduce unnecessary token use
✅ How to create a Mission Control dashboard and connect your agents to it
✅ How to export Pine Script and verify strategy results in TradingView
✅ How to connect TradingView alerts and webhooks to Trigger.trade
✅ Why forward testing matters before committing money to a strategy
✅ What five years of automated trading have taught me

videos.title: This Robot Looks DEMONIC... On Purpose?
videos.summary_source_text:
This Robot Looks DEMONIC... On Purpose? This robot looks straight up like a fantasy movie villain, but it was designed like that on purpose.

Despite how it looks, the Threehalves robot's design actually makes perfect sense: four legs for stability, tools that attach directly to its wrists, and horns that house cameras for a remote operator.

The goal is to let skilled workers tackle dangerous jobs from a safe distance, like wildfire zones, collapsed buildings, and toxic environments.

It’s still a half-built proof of concept. But this is the kind of robotics idea I want to see work. Even if I’d absolutely run the other way if I saw it in the woods.

Who stood out in the first game of the preseason as we get closer to opening night on the 29th? videos.summary_source_text:
3 Edge Drags Every Hockey Player Must Practice The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: Google Gemini Spark Is INSANE: Your 24/7 AI Agent Explained
videos.summary_source_text:
Google Gemini Spark Is INSANE: Your 24/7 AI Agent Explained Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/

Google says Gemini Spark can keep working after you close your laptop and lock your phone — running tasks on Google's servers for hours or even days without waiting for another prompt.

But there's a very specific point where that autonomy stops.

Gemini Spark is Google's "24/7 personal AI agent," powered by Gemini 3.8 Flash through the Antigravity framework. Unlike a normal chatbot that answers a question and waits, Spark can plan a multi-step task, interact with connected apps, browse the web, and keep working until it either finishes or reaches something that requires your approval.

The system revolves around three controls: Tasks, Schedules, and Skills. A Task defines what Spark should accomplish. A Schedule determines when it runs — including recurring timers, Gmail-based triggers, and topic monitors. Skills give Spark reusable instructions, like learning your email style from previous messages and applying it to future drafts.

Put those together and Spark starts looking less like another Gemini feature and more like an automation layer across your digital life.

It can work with Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Keep, Tasks, and Google Photos, while third-party integrations can extend it to services including Canva, Dropbox, Instacart, OpenTable, and Zillow through the Model Context Protocol.

Then there's web browsing.

Spark has both local and remote browsing modes. Local mode can use your actual Chrome session, including sites you're already logged into, but your computer needs to remain on. Remote mode runs inside Google's infrastructure, allowing a task to continue even when your own device is offline.

That's also where Google's biggest guardrails become obvious.

Spark can research flights, compare prices, navigate websites, and get you most of the way through a transaction. But when it reaches a login it doesn't have, a payment, or another sensitive action requiring confirmation, it stops and hands control back to you. It can get to checkout. It won't independently cross it.

We also break down the prompt structure that gets better results: clearly specify the source, the output you want, and — for recurring automations — the schedule. That can mean an 8 AM Gmail task digest, a weekly Drive check, a research report saved directly into Google Docs, or a reusable Skill based on your own writing.

Access has limits too. According to Google's rollout described here, Spark requires Google AI Pro or Ultra, a personal account, and users must be 18 or older. Availability and individual features also vary by region.

And Spark isn't the same thing as Gemini chat, Deep Research, Gems, or Scheduled Actions. Those tools can answer, research, customize conversations, or trigger timed actions. Spark is designed around persistent, multi-step execution across apps.

That makes the most important question less about whether Spark is "autonomous" and more about where Google has deliberately decided autonomy should end.

Because the number that matters isn't 24/7.

It's the confirmation prompt.

09:55 So Is It Actually Worth Turning On?

videos.summary_source_text:
How to Do More Pullups in Your NEXT Set (GUARANTEED!) Want to do more pullups? Whether you can currently do 2 pullups, 5 pullups, 10 pullups or you're trying to reach 15, 20 or even 25 unbroken reps, the fastest way to increase pullups is not simply trying harder on every set. In this video, I’m going to show you exactly how to do more pullups by fixing six common mistakes that make every rep harder than it needs to be.

Do more pullups with programs here - https://athleanx.com
Subscribe To This Channel Here - http://bit.ly/2b0coMW

If you’ve been searching for how to increase pullups, how to get better at pullups, how to improve pullup strength or how to do more pullups in a row, this is where you want to start. Most people assume their problem is a lack of back strength. Sometimes it is. But very often the bigger issue is inefficient setup, wasted movement, poor body position and failing to use the strongest muscles possible to perform the exercise.

The first mistake is starting the pullup too loose. Hanging passively from the bar can create instability through the shoulders and shoulder blades, forcing you to waste energy before the rep even begins. Instead, engage the lats before you pull. Think about creating a slight backward angle rather than simply hanging straight down. This helps set the shoulder blades, turns on the lats and puts you in a much stronger position to initiate every rep.

Next, look at your elbows. If your elbows are directly in line with your body when viewed from the side, you may be missing a better pulling position. Getting the elbows slightly out in front places the shoulder closer to the scapular plane, gives the lats a better stretch and helps you produce more pulling strength while keeping the shoulder in a more comfortable position.

The third mistake might be the biggest reason you can’t do more pullups: energy leaks. If your legs are dangling, your knees are bent, your feet are crossed behind you and your body is moving around under the bar, you are making yourself feel heavier. Keep your legs together, knees straight, quads tight, glutes squeezed, core braced and feet slightly out in front. This creates one rigid line of force and can instantly make pullups feel easier.

Mistake number four is what you are doing with your hands. A shoulder-width grip is a strong starting point, but the real key is the direction of force. Instead of only thinking about pulling straight down on the bar, think about pulling down AND inward at the same time. Squeezing the hands toward each other while you pull can recruit more of the muscles that help adduct the arms and create a stronger, more stable pull.

The fifth mistake is attacking the bar with the wrong target. Stop thinking only about getting your chin over the bar. Instead, think about driving the upper sternum toward the bar. Reaching with the chest rather than collapsing forward with the chin helps keep your torso open, your back engaged and your line of pull more efficient. You do not have to touch your chest to the bar. The goal is to use the sternum as your target so you stay tight and powerful.

Finally, if you really want to know how to do more pullups, you have to stop treating pullups differently from every other strength exercise. Progressive overload matters. Just as you would add weight to a bench press to get stronger, weighted pullups can help build the strength needed to make bodyweight pullups easier. Add weight for lower-rep sets, then remove the weight and immediately perform bodyweight reps as a drop set. Over time, your weighted reps and bodyweight pullup numbers can climb together.

So if you have ever asked how to do more pullups, how to increase pullups fast, how to get better at pullups, how to improve pullup form, how to build pullup strength, how to increase pullup reps or how to do 20 pullups, start with these six corrections. Fix your setup. Engage the lats. Get the elbows in the right position. Eliminate energy leaks. Pull down and in. Lead with the sternum. Then add weighted pullups to progressively build strength.

The goal is simple: make every rep more efficient, then build the specific pulling strength needed to increase your pullup max.

Pullups are one of the best bodyweight exercises for building your back, lats, biceps, grip and upper body. The stronger and more technically sound you become, the easier it is to add reps and break through a pullup plateau.

videos.title: Anthropic Researcher Quits With A Terrifying AI Warning
videos.summary_source_text:
Anthropic Researcher Quits With A Terrifying AI Warning Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/

Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon just resigned after saying his former employer is “far and away” the most responsible company in the AI race. He also says Anthropic isn’t cutting safety corners. So why walk away before his equity even started vesting?

The answer is more complicated than the headlines calling Coxon Anthropic’s “safety chief” or a “whistleblower.” He was a pretraining researcher who worked inside frontier AI development at both OpenAI and Anthropic, including research tied to GPT-4o. His warning isn’t that Anthropic has secretly abandoned safety. It’s that competitive pressure could eventually make even the most cautious AI lab move faster than it believes is safe.

And the timing matters.

Five days earlier, OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra, posting major benchmark results including 99.9% on ARC-AGI-3 and 97.6% on FrontierMath Tier 4. OpenAI president Greg Brockman said it was “not unreasonable” to feel we are entering the AGI era — but OpenAI’s official launch materials did not formally classify Astra as AGI.

The more consequential detail may be cybersecurity. Under OpenAI’s Preparedness Framework, Astra was classified “Critical” for cyber capability after controlled tests where it autonomously discovered vulnerabilities and constructed exploit chains against hardened targets.

But that comparison needs context. An independent evaluator recorded zero successful attacks against fully hardened targets, and Astra failed all seven of the hardest “Elite” challenges it faced. “Critical” describes a specific capability threshold — not a model capable of hacking anything on demand.

That tension leads directly to Coxon’s deeper concern: recursive AI development.

Frontier models are already getting better at coding, debugging machine-learning systems, optimizing training infrastructure, and automating pieces of AI research. If AI increasingly helps build the next generation of AI, development cycles could accelerate — potentially creating systems that become harder to monitor or control.

But the evidence also shows an important limitation. OpenAI’s own safety evaluation says Astra does NOT reach its “High AI Self-Improvement” threshold and cannot independently design and execute frontier-scale AI training. On RE-Bench, AI agents can outperform humans on short research tasks, while humans regain a major advantage when given much longer time horizons.

So the real argument isn’t whether runaway self-improvement has already arrived. It’s what happens if competitive pressure pushes AI labs toward that point faster than their safety processes can handle.

Anthropic itself has argued that voluntary corporate promises may ultimately be insufficient and that governments could need authority to stop deployments presenting serious catastrophic risks. Meanwhile, an autonomous-agent cybersecurity incident involving an early Claude Opus build illustrates the paradox: increasingly capable systems can create unexpected failures, while responsible monitoring can still catch and investigate them.

Coxon’s resignation doesn’t provide a smoking gun or a neat ending. Instead, it raises a harder question: if even researchers inside the companies they consider most responsible are worried about where the race leads, who ultimately decides how quickly frontier AI should move?

videos.title: Evade Defenders Without Fully Stopping Your Momentum
videos.summary_source_text:
Evade Defenders Without Fully Stopping Your Momentum The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

Your blood contains only a surprisingly small amount of glucose at any given time. Even with about 5 liters of blood circulating through your body, normal blood glucose amounts to roughly a teaspoon of sugar. In diabetes, it’s closer to 2 teaspoons, so even a relatively small increase can make a significant difference.

Blood sugar levels can look normal for years before diabetes develops. Insulin’s primary job is to remove sugar from the blood. This means the body may be producing more and more insulin to keep blood sugar under control long before glucose levels become obviously elevated.

Normal fasting insulin levels vary from country to country and are often based on population averages. The problem is that if a large portion of the population already has insulin resistance, an “average” insulin level may not necessarily reflect optimal metabolic health.

A fasting insulin test is one of the best ways to detect insulin resistance early. Focus on getting your fasting insulin below 5, reducing sugar intake, and avoiding frequent snacking.

videos.summary_source_text:
The Healthiest Carbohydrate in the World! The safest carbohydrates are non-starchy vegetables because they contain very little sugar or starch and a lot of fiber. Unlike sugar and starch, fiber does not break down into glucose and has very little effect on insulin.

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/4xr3z5I

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements. 

Carbohydrates come in three forms:
• Sugar
• Starch
• Fiber

Starch is essentially chains of sugar molecules, which is why foods like bread can quickly start tasting sweet as enzymes in your mouth break the starch down.

Non-starchy vegetables like broccoli sit very low on the glycemic index because they’re high in fiber and low in starch. This makes them one of the best carbohydrate choices for keeping blood sugar and insulin more stable.

videos.title: The #1 Mineral Deficiency in High Blood Pressure (Hypertension)
videos.summary_source_text:
The #1 Mineral Deficiency in High Blood Pressure (Hypertension) Potassium is one of the most important minerals when it comes to your blood pressure. You need at least 4700 milligrams of potassium per day. People with the highest sodium combined with the lowest potassium intake have a much higher risk of heart attack.

Watch the FULL video here: ▶️https://youtu.be/Qgwu_-6wy40

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/3VsAkkS

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements. 

What should you eat to get more potassium?

* Avocado: about 700 mg per avocado
* Wild salmon: about 970 mg per serving

Potassium helps relax your blood vessels. When potassium is low, blood vessels stay more constricted, and the artery walls become stiffer.

videos.title: 7 Puck Control Techniques Every Hockey Player Should Practice
videos.summary_source_text:
7 Puck Control Techniques Every Hockey Player Should Practice The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: xAI SKIPPED Grok 4.7… Here’s What’s Coming Instead
videos.summary_source_text:
xAI SKIPPED Grok 4.7… Here’s What’s Coming Instead Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/

Grok 4.7 was built to persist through difficult, long-running tasks. According to Elon Musk, its reinforcement learning may have accidentally taught it to do the opposite: give up early.

Then, before Grok 4.7 even shipped, Musk started talking about Grok 4.8 — a reportedly 2.5-trillion-parameter model trained on a brand-new C++ software stack. That raises a bigger question: is xAI genuinely accelerating toward the frontier, or are the model numbers moving faster than the evidence?

Grok 4.6 gives us the clearest baseline. Released August 12, 2026, it brought a 500,000-token context window, configurable reasoning, text and image input, function calling, structured output, and aggressive API pricing at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens.

xAI also reported meaningful gains across agentic benchmarks. Grok 4.6 reached 69.9% on CursorBench, 65.9% on DeepSWE, 57.5% on APEX-Agents, and 26% on Terminal-Bench 3.0. That last result is especially important because xAI's roadmap has increasingly focused on models that can keep working through complex engineering and professional tasks rather than simply producing better chatbot answers.

Grok 4.7 was supposed to push that further. Musk described it as roughly 2.1 trillion parameters, compared with approximately 1.5 trillion for 4.6. But its release window slipped repeatedly. On September 11, Musk finally gave a technical explanation: reinforcement learning may have penalized long answers too aggressively, causing the model to abandon difficult problems early and insufficiently check its own work.

That's almost the exact opposite of what a persistent AI agent needs.

And that's where Grok 4.8 enters the story.

On September 13, Musk described Grok 4.8 as a 2.5-trillion-parameter model running on a new low-level software stack. But there is an important catch: parameter counts aren't necessarily directly comparable. Grok-1, for example, used a mixture-of-experts architecture where only part of its total parameter count was active for each token. Without architectural details for Grok 4.8, 2.5 trillion tells us much less about real inference compute or capability than it initially appears to.

The potentially bigger development is xAI's software stack. Musk has previously discussed an in-house low-level training stack designed for enormous GPU clusters and claimed major performance advantages over JAX on very large runs. The engineering idea is plausible; the claimed magnitude has not been independently demonstrated.

That matters because xAI's compute story isn't simply about owning GPUs. Colossus has expanded dramatically, but efficiently coordinating huge numbers of accelerators — especially across infrastructure and networking constraints — is its own engineering problem. A better training stack could potentially matter more than adding another trillion parameters.

Meanwhile, the competitive bar keeps moving. GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, and Gemini 3.8 Flash are all part of the landscape Grok's next models have to compete against.

This video separates what xAI has actually shipped from what Musk has announced, explains what went wrong with Grok 4.7, breaks down what the 2.5-trillion-parameter Grok 4.8 claim really tells us, and looks at why xAI's new C++ stack may ultimately be the more important story.

videos.title: Gemini 3.8 LIVE is INSANE: Google's New AI Can Think WHILE It Talks
videos.summary_source_text:
Gemini 3.8 LIVE is INSANE: Google's New AI Can Think WHILE It Talks Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/

Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking just hit 82.6 on Artificial Analysis’ Speech-to-Speech Quality Index — edging out OpenAI’s closest comparable realtime voice model. But the benchmark isn’t the most interesting part. Google says this model can actually “think while talking.”

That sounds far more human than what’s really happening.

Google launched two models: Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking. Both are built on the Gemini 3 Pro architecture and use native audio-to-audio processing, taking audio, images, and video directly in while streaming speech back out — instead of relying on the traditional speech-to-text → language model → text-to-speech pipeline.

That architecture brings some serious upgrades: roughly 1.18-second time to first spoken word for standard Live, barge-in support, 97+ languages, mid-conversation language switching, and a massive 131,072-token input context window.

Vision is now part of the conversation too. Google demonstrated Gemini tracking a physical chess board through a live camera, turning a hand-drawn UI sketch into React code, and interacting with content inside products like Docs and Gmail.

Then there’s Extended Thinking.

Google describes it as reasoning and speaking simultaneously, but the underlying mechanism is more precise. The model can give you an interim spoken response while its interaction remains “IN_PROGRESS,” continue an asynchronous search or function call in the background, and then resume speaking when that work finishes. Developers can even control the reasoning level through `thinking_config`.

So this isn’t a model literally maintaining two human-like trains of thought at once. It’s an asynchronous architecture designed to eliminate the awkward silence that normally appears while an AI works on a more complicated task.

And the benchmark results reveal why that matters.

Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking scores 82.6 on Artificial Analysis’ Speech-to-Speech Quality Index, compared with 81.5 for GPT-Live-1 “Astra.” But on τ-Voice — a benchmark focused on completing multi-step tasks through voice — Extended Thinking reaches 68.6% versus just 30.1% for standard Gemini 3.8 Live.

That jump may be much more important than the headline voice-quality score.

There’s also a major price difference between the modes. Standard Gemini 3.8 Live works out to roughly $0.84 per hour of audio based on Artificial Analysis’ pricing methodology, while Extended Thinking sits around $3.50 per hour because of the additional reasoning compute.

Best Way To Get Better At Hockey Without Icetime or Practicing The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: Use This Effortless Swing Tip To Hit Driver Further
videos.summary_source_text:
Use This Effortless Swing Tip To Hit Driver Further Want to hit driver further without making a longer or harder golf swing?

In this Danny Maude golf lesson, you’ll learn how to create more clubhead speed, improve your driver strike and generate effortless power with a surprisingly short golf swing.

This golf swing lesson is especially useful for senior golfers, golfers with limited mobility, anyone struggling with flexibility, or golfers who feel they have to make a huge backswing to hit driver longer.

Danny Maude explains two simple ideas that can completely change how you create speed with the driver: knowing exactly where your body needs to finish, and learning how to “catapult” the golf club through impact at the right moment.

In this golf lesson, you’ll learn:

• How to hit driver further with a short backswing
• How to create more clubhead speed without swinging harder
• The correct driver setup for better launch and distance
• Why your trail shoulder position matters through impact
• How to stop lunging towards the golf ball
• Why some golfers lose speed by over-rotating through impact
• How to use the Longest Putt golf drill with driver
• How to use sound to improve golf swing speed
• Why an underarm throwing action can improve your driver swing
• How to create effortless power even with limited flexibility

If you struggle to hit driver consistently, lack distance off the tee or feel you need a longer backswing to create more power, this simple golf drill can help you experience where speed really comes from.

The goal isn’t to force a bigger swing.

It’s to improve your strike, give your body a clear destination and learn how to accelerate the golf club through impact while staying behind the golf ball.

Practice Plan

Most golfers trying to stop coming over the top are working on their arms or their hips — but the real fix is in the trail shoulder  position on the way down. Watch how Tiger Woods and Justin Thomas get the trail shoulder tilt steeper on the way down than on the way back — roughly 40 degrees in the backswing and 55 degrees through impact — and how the club across shoulders drill gives any golfer the same feel immediately. If you leave this video without trying the club across shoulders drill, you're leaving solid contact and correct golf shaft lean on the table.

• Why the trail shoulder golf swing position going up and back in the backswing means it must go down and forward on the way down
• How a high trail shoulder in the downswing creates a steep club path and causes you to come over the top
• Why the trail shoulder must reach 55 degrees of tilt through impact — steeper than the 40 degrees in the backswing
• How Tiger Woods and Justin Thomas use trail shoulder tilt to produce correct golf shaft lean and inside-out club path
• The club across shoulders drill for training the correct amount of trail shoulder depth and forward rotation
• Why the right-side oblique crunch and trail knee forward are the two key feels for getting the trail shoulder down correctly
• How getting the trail shoulder down and forward moves the low point forward for better golf impact position and shaft lean
• Why the trail arm staying slightly bent through impact prevents fat shots when the trail shoulder goes down correctly

Around 25–40% of the weight loss experienced with Ozempic is muscle loss. Once you stop Ozempic and the weight returns, much of it is fat.

Most GLP-1 drugs work directly on the brain, essentially stopping hunger, while also slowing digestion. This means much of the weight loss from GLP-1s comes from simply eating less.

GLP-1 drugs can also leave you with nutritional deficiencies. Other Ozempic side effects include gastroparesis, acid reflux, vision loss, hair loss, diarrhea, and pancreatitis.

Muscle loss is one of the biggest concerns after taking Ozempic. To help prevent and correct muscle loss, focus on resistance training along with getting enough leucine, a key amino acid for muscle growth found in high-quality animal protein.

A low-carb diet paired with intermittent fasting is one of the healthiest ways to lose weight.

videos.title: 18.09.26 - Ep.24 - The Science of Risk Management
videos.summary_source_text:
18.09.26 - Ep.24 - The Science of Risk Management In Episode 24 of RIFT Before You Quit, we move from the psychology of elite traders into one of the most important foundations of professional trading and investing: risk management.

Making money in the markets is only part of the equation. The ability to protect capital, control exposure and remain in the game long enough to compound is what separates disciplined market participants from those who allow individual decisions to determine their entire financial future.

🛡️ CAPITAL PRESERVATION COMES FIRST

Professional investors don't begin by asking, "How much can I make?"

They ask:

What can go wrong?
How much capital is exposed?
What is the probability of loss?
How large could the loss become?
How will this position affect the rest of the portfolio?
Can the portfolio continue if the trade fails?

Returns attract capital, but risk management preserves it.

A trader can generate impressive returns and still damage their capital through excessive drawdowns. Episode 24 explores why consistency, survivability and controlled exposure matter more than chasing individual winning trades.

📐 POSITION SIZING

One of the fundamental principles of risk management is that risk determines position size — not confidence or excitement.

We examine practical position-sizing calculations, including how a trader can determine the appropriate number of units based on:

Total portfolio value
Maximum percentage risk
Entry price
Risk level or stop-loss
Risk per unit

For example, with a $100,000 portfolio and a 1% maximum risk, the trader may accept a $1,000 loss. If the difference between entry and risk level represents $5 per unit, the position size would be 200 units.

The important principle is simple:

Your position should be determined by the amount you are prepared to lose — not by how much you hope to make.

🧮 THE KELLY CRITERION

We also explore the Kelly Criterion, originally developed within information theory and later applied to capital allocation.

The framework considers factors such as:

Probability of winning
Probability of losing
Potential payoff
Available edge
Appropriate capital allocation

Having an edge does not mean going all-in.

We examine the Kelly paradox, the dangers of overbetting, and why fractional Kelly approaches can be considered when full Kelly exposure would create excessive volatility or drawdown.

⚠️ RISK OF RUIN

A strategy can have positive expected returns and still fail if too much capital is placed at risk.

This leads into the concept of risk of ruin and the importance of understanding:

Losing streaks
Drawdowns
Position size
Recovery requirements
Capital reserves
Portfolio survival

The objective isn't simply to survive one bad trade. It is to build a process capable of surviving an extended sequence of adverse outcomes.

📊 LEVERAGE & EXPOSURE

Leverage can dramatically increase market exposure relative to available capital.

We examine why traders need to understand the relationship between:

Margin → Position Size → Exposure → Volatility → Drawdown → Liquidation Risk

The key principle is:

Risk follows exposure, not intention.

A trader may believe they are risking a small amount of capital, while their actual market exposure is substantially larger.

🌐 PORTFOLIO & CORRELATION RISK

One position might appear to carry only 1% risk. But several positions can become a much larger risk when they are correlated.

Five different assets can still represent one underlying trade if they are all exposed to the same sector, narrative, technology, market condition or economic factor.

This is why professional risk management looks beyond individual trades and considers the entire portfolio.

🏦 THE FIVE LEVELS OF INSTITUTIONAL RISK

We examine five layers of risk management:

Trader Risk – decisions, discipline and execution
Portfolio Risk – concentration and correlation
Market Risk – volatility and adverse price movement
Liquidity Risk – the ability to enter or exit positions
Systematic Risk – broader economic or market-wide events

Understanding these layers changes the way a trader thinks about capital.

✅ FROM THEORY TO PRACTICAL TRADING

The episode concludes by moving toward a practical trading framework: creating Standard Operating Procedures and pre-trade checklists.

Just as financial platforms use verification steps to reduce avoidable mistakes, professional traders can use structured processes before entering positions.

The goal is simple:

Be calculative. Be precise. Be disciplined.

Before focusing on how much you can make, understand how much you can afford to lose.

This is the science of risk management.

videos.title: Avalanche Training Camp Gets Underway. Ball Arena Getting $135 Million in Upgrades.
videos.summary_source_text:
Avalanche Training Camp Gets Underway. Ball Arena Getting $135 Million in Upgrades. Colorado Avalanche fans get their first look at fresh line combinations and a driverless Zamboni as training camp kicks off. Are preseason shakeups and cutting-edge tech setting the stage for an electrifying season? Chris Micieli and Zach Pearson break down standout moments from camp, including coach Jared Bednar’s high praise for Mackenzie Blackwood and intriguing opportunities for prospects like Beckett Hamilton. Is Blackwood poised to seize the starting goalie spot, and which young players could vault up the depth chart?

Ball Arena is primed for $135 million in upgrades, sparking debate on how the new amenities could enhance fan experience, from expanded atriums to faster concourse navigation and premium seating options. Plus, the hosts challenge themselves to say nice things about the Vegas Golden Knights—does T-Mobile Arena really deliver the NHL’s best in-game production? Get the inside scoop on the Colorado Avalanche’s latest moves and the evolving Western Conference landscape.

videos.summary_source_text:
The Right Elbow Impact Position Drill Comment "BRICK" for the lowest price on the Blue Brick!

If you can't hit draws, it's not your swing plane it's actually your right elbow.

This video breaks down why your right arm gets "over the top" in transition, killing your window at impact and causing pulls and slices. You'll learn exactly where tour players position their trail elbow at impact and the simple one-handed drill to feel it yourself.

After watching, you'll know how to create the biggest possible "window" between your elbows at impact, get the club coming from the inside, and start compressing the ball for real draws instead of slices.

We used the Blue Brick as visual feedback to confirm the club is swinging from the inside while you groove the elbow position.

Like this video if you're trying this drill, and check the link in my bio for the Blue Brick.
