videos.summary_source_text:
This Is Why You Struggle With Skating Backwards The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: Why Is The Rocker Crucial For Speed?
videos.summary_source_text:
Why Is The Rocker Crucial For Speed? The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: OpenAI GPT-7 LEAK: “BEL” 10T Parameter the Next Massive Leap
videos.summary_source_text:
OpenAI GPT-7 LEAK: “BEL” 10T Parameter the Next Massive Leap Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/

GPT-7 is reportedly already training. More than 10 trillion parameters. An internal codename: “Bel.” And potentially the foundation for an AGI-threshold model.

There’s just one problem: none of it has been confirmed.

The entire “Bel” story traces back to a single anonymous account, @synthwavedd, which claimed on August 25, 2026 that OpenAI had finished pretraining a massive model positioned beyond its current generation. The rumor quickly spread across tech Twitter, Reddit, YouTube, and international tech press — despite the original source openly describing the information as rumor and speculation.

Meanwhile, the model that actually exists, GPT-6 Astra, is already doing things that would have sounded extreme a generation ago.

Astra reportedly has a 1.05 million-token context window, supports outputs up to 128,000 tokens, and reaches 99.9% on ARC-AGI-3 with chain-of-thought reasoning enabled. Its OSWorld performance jumped to 72.6%, and on one cybersecurity exploit benchmark it went from solving 42.4% of challenges to 100% when time limits were removed.

But those numbers hide some important limitations.

Long-horizon autonomy remains a major problem. Hallucinations have been reduced, not eliminated. Agents can lose track of earlier decisions, make planning errors, and still require humans inside the loop for extended tasks. And Astra’s reported decline in “monitorability” raises an even more complicated question: what happens when increasingly autonomous AI systems become harder to observe while they reason?

That’s where the idea of a true GPT-7-level leap becomes much more interesting than a parameter count.

A genuinely new generation would need to move beyond being a powerful chatbot with tools. Persistent memory, reliable multi-day planning, broader multimodality, end-to-end digital work, and potentially AI systems capable of contributing meaningfully to AI research itself would represent a much bigger shift.

OpenAI has publicly discussed that last frontier. The company says an automated research intern is already assisting its scientists, while fully automated AI researchers have been discussed as a target for 2028.

Then there’s the money.

OpenAI’s Stargate initiative involves a planned $500 billion infrastructure buildout targeting roughly 10 gigawatts of AI data-center capacity in the US. Add major NVIDIA and AMD compute agreements, enormous funding commitments, and reported cloud spending, and the infrastructure being assembled for future AI systems is arguably more interesting than the “Bel” rumor itself.

The competitive pressure is also intensifying. Anthropic, Google DeepMind, xAI, and Chinese AI labs including Alibaba and Baidu are all pushing different approaches to frontier models, multimodality, agents, reasoning, and massive-scale compute.

So could OpenAI eventually train something on the scale being attributed to “Bel”? The infrastructure makes increasingly large systems plausible.

But that doesn’t make the leak real.

In this video, we trace the original GPT-7 “Bel” claim, examine what GPT-6 Astra can actually do, break down where current AI agents still fail, and look at what a genuine generational leap beyond Astra would need to accomplish.

Because the biggest story may not be an alleged 10-trillion-parameter model at all. It may be what OpenAI is publicly building toward — and how close the industry really is to AI systems that no longer need humans constantly standing inside the loop.

videos.title: You WON’T believe what my Official handicap is…
videos.summary_source_text:
You WON’T believe what my Official handicap is… Rick Shiels plays Tyler Gordon, a 16-year-old off +2 and the top-ranked junior golfer in Scotland, in the final episode of the Handicap Series. One of the best young players in the country plays against a PGA pro, and at the end of it all, Rick reveals his real handicap for the first time.

Check out Tyler on Instagram!
https://www.instagram.com/tylergordongolf

👋 WELCOME — I’M RICK SHIELS

This channel is all about helping you play better golf and enjoy the game more.
I make videos for every type of golfer: beginners, weekend players, improving golfers, and low handicaps chasing new personal bests.

Here’s what you’ll find on the channel:

⭐ GOLF COACHING & LESSONS

I share simple, practical and proven golf instruction designed to help you:

• Fix your slice
• Fix your hook
• Hit your driver longer and straighter
• Improve your iron strike
• Add height, control and distance
• Learn how to draw and fade the golf ball
• Improve ball position, alignment and setup
• Build a repeatable, consistent golf swing
• Increase clubhead speed
• Improve swing path and club face control

You’ll also find full swing analysis, beginner advice, drills you can try at the range, and tips for getting better at golf quickly.

⭐ SHORT GAME & PUTTING

Lower your scores with short-game tips that help you:

• Stop duffing and thinning chips
• Improve contact and distance control
• Pitch closer to the hole
• Create more backspin
• Build confidence around the greens
• Read putts better
• Improve pace control and holing-out percentages

Short game is where most golfers drop shots — so I make sure you have everything you need to get better fast.

⭐ GOLF EQUIPMENT REVIEWS (H.I.T)

I test the latest:

• Drivers
• Irons
• Putters
• Wedges
• Golf balls
• Launch monitors
• Golf gadgets
• Budget vs premium clubs

All reviews are completely honest and independent. I use Trackman and GCQuad to give you accurate numbers you can trust.

If you’re trying to find the best golf driver, best irons, most forgiving clubs or value golf equipment — you’re in the right place.

⭐ BREAK 75 & GOLF ENTERTAINMENT

Break 75 has become one of YouTube’s biggest golf series.
You’ll see:

• Full 18-hole course vlogs
• Course management strategies
• Matches against tour players and creators
• Pressure moments, birdie runs and disaster holes
• Some of the world’s best golf courses
• Real, relatable golf

I also play matches and challenges with some of the biggest names in golf, including:

• Bryson DeChambeau
• Peter Finch
• Good Good
• GM Golf
• Bob Does Sports
• BustaJack
• Grant Horvat
• Me and My Golf
• Danny Maude

These help bring you the most entertaining and competitive golf content possible.

⭐ TRAVEL & COURSE VLOGS

I film at some of the most incredible golf destinations around the world. Expect:

• Amazing golf courses
• Behind-the-scenes access
• Player interactions
• Travel insights
• Bucket-list destinations
• Worldwide golf adventures

⭐ THE GOAL

To make golf more fun, more accessible and help you become a better, more confident, happier golfer — whether you’re breaking 100 or trying to break par.
